mode: Experience with game selection and feedback/signature Operate moments
scope: Hero held .20/.28/.35/.50 plus clean B arrival

method.browser: Fresh isolated Playwright Chromium contexts, /usr/bin/chromium, SwiftShader
method.hero_wait: Actual published canvas progress/entrance, then completion fence newer than scroll request at the four requested held points
limits: No mobile or video, per scope
Shared-event service unavailable in this local QA context; no production-availability conclusion

design_specificity: Strongly specific to Yeonseok and Lisbeth. The portraits, exact countries/cities, InterPals/awkwardness/twelve-hour story, thirteen-hour clock, playful room reactions and letter/signature/rose ending cannot be transferred to an unrelated product unchanged. Its weakness is continuity and composition, not generic content.

heuristics.name: Visibility of System Status
heuristics.reason: Gallery selection, clock preview, signature readiness/confirmation and saved feedback respond clearly. The Hero loses its editorial cues before arrival and supplies little orientation during the image handoff.

heuristics.name: Match Between System and Real World
heuristics.reason: The language is specifically for this couple: InterPals, the awkward beginning, twelve continuous hours, Gwangju/Santo Domingo, thirteen hours, family domino play and the personal letter. The relationship date stays separate from first-contact copy.

heuristics.name: User Control and Freedom
heuristics.reason: Direct games/letter navigation, optional pact, fold/reread, shared-panel Escape and continue-alone exits work. No task trap observed.

heuristics.name: Consistency and Standards
heuristics.reason: Controls behave consistently, but the full-frame double exposure at Hero p=.35 and the jump from richly rendered B to a flat thread diagram weaken the promised continuous world.

heuristics.name: Error Prevention
heuristics.reason: Empty feedback cannot submit; textarea has a 4000-character limit; the signature requires a meaningful stroke and explicit commit. Optional name signing is disclosed as text.

heuristics.name: Recognition Rather Than Recall
heuristics.reason: Named navigation and eight labeled game buttons keep routes visible. Seven tiny unlabeled inactive sculptures are hard to identify by sight, so users fall back to the text list.

heuristics.name: Flexibility and Efficiency of Use
heuristics.reason: Games/letter shortcuts bypass long reading, gallery arrow keys work, language persists correctly through feedback-to-home-to-game, and reread works. Applicable because the review includes game selection and simple forms.

heuristics.name: Aesthetic and Minimalist Design
heuristics.reason: The opening and personal art are strong; ghosted transition imagery, repeated left-copy/right-art chapters and small inactive gallery pieces create uneven craft and rhythm.

heuristics.name: Error Recovery
heuristics.reason: The observed unavailable shared-event service gives a plain-language connection error and a working continue-alone/Escape exit. Source feedback recovery preserves input and offers retry copy; a forced backend-error test was not run.

heuristics.name: Help and Documentation
heuristics.reason: Clock input, signature instructions, typed alternative, local-storage note, feedback empty state/demo limits and game-entry explanation are concise and contextual. Applicable because these are actual interactive tasks, not only a passive experience.

applicability: All ten apply to the reviewed mixed surface: game selection, signature and feedback provide real efficiency, prevention, recovery and contextual-help tasks. No irrelevant dashboard/bulk-action requirements were imposed.

checklist.evidence: One primary reading/selection task per chapter; letter prose has a clear centered reading surface.
Eight sibling game choices form one semantic selection group, despite being laid out over two rows.
Clocks/preview cities, game art/selection/start and pact controls remain colocated.
Stable chapter states have a dominant image, numeral or title; the p=.35 transition exception is recorded separately as A1.
Pact/signing and optional shared controls disclose after opening; the principal letter is readable first.
The game-selection decision exposes eight alternatives.
Chosen time is restated in the duel chapter; selected game name/subtitle stays by its start action.
Shared workbench, pact and typed-signature fallback open only when requested.

decision_points_over_four.reason: Eight game identities in the native gallery and labeled chooser; the selected-game start button is a subsequent action, not a ninth game.

cognitive_load.top_level_nav: Three destinations; the two-language switch is a separate preference decision, not five equivalent destination choices.

strengths: The opening and approved B room deliver a warm recognizable portrait of the actual couple, with faces and outfits reading clearly at both desktop sizes.

Story truth is specific and naturally ordered: InterPals → awkward/rude start → twelve continuous hours, followed by distance/time and playful competition. April4 is not presented as first-contact date.

The ending is substantive and functional: one readable letter, an optional real drawn signature, browser-local disclosure, a completed rose scene with signed-pact copy, and a working reread. Feedback has an honest local-only note and visible saved confirmation.

emotional_journey.opening: Immediate intimate recognition and visual richness.
emotional_journey.first_valley: Couple disappears at .28 and two worlds ghost together at .35, weakening presence before B.
emotional_journey.arrival: Full B room restores familiarity and warmth.
emotional_journey.middle: The thin InterPals thread and repeated split layouts reduce energy; clocks, bird greeting and actual reaction choice supply useful small participatory moments.
emotional_journey.peak_end: The actual letter and personal commitment have the strongest emotional content. Drawing and committing a signature led to the pact-aware received-rose line; reread worked.
emotional_journey.recommendation: Spend the next visual effort on spatial continuity and the middle chapter rhythm. Preserve the letter/pact/rose chain.

priority_issues.title: The central Hero handoff becomes an image disappearance and full-frame dissolve
evidence: held-hero-p02-ko-1440.png: p=.2000, original standing couple remains.
held-hero-p028-ko-1440.png: p=.2800, couple has disappeared; cosmic background fills the screen without B.
held-hero-p035-ko-1440.png: p=.3500, telescope, candles, planets and floor overlap the room characters, desks and rabbit in a full-frame double exposure.
held-hero-p05-ko-1440.png: p=.5000, clean approved B room finally fills the frame.
held-hero-states.json records frameSerial, actual progress, camera, surface state and GPU completion fence for all four frames.
priority_issues.impact: The signature journey is where the site should feel most authored. Its held middle has two incompatible perspective systems and no stable spatial focal point, making the room feel revealed by a slideshow transition.
priority_issues.fix: Keep the approved B arrival and original portrait/art intact. Design the intermediate camera/aperture compositions backward from B; use geometric occlusion and one readable depth opening rather than whole-frame opacity mixing. Keep the couple spatially present until the opening genuinely hides or replaces them; do not add reconstructed faces or a second renderer. Validate these same four held positions before motion tuning.

priority_issues.title: Seven of eight game sculptures are too small to carry the visual choice
evidence: 10-gallery-ko-1440.png: selected domino is about 170×330px; many inactive pieces occupy only about 45–70px in their larger dimension.
17-gallery-es-1920.png: the camel is prominent while the inactive deck, drawing card, cover, headphones and house remain small satellites. All eight names are visible below.
priority_issues.impact: A user can complete the choice with the labels, but the intended collectible gallery mostly functions as one showcase object plus a text menu. Small dark headphones and cards are especially hard to recognize.
priority_issues.fix: Preserve the native curated gallery and its eight identities. Increase inactive-object scale and scene occupancy, reduce the selected/inactive size ratio, and give hover/focus a nearby game name. Retain the current labeled keyboard choices and single start action; do not convert it to a card grid.

priority_issues.title: The rich room gives way to an overly sparse, repeated story layout
evidence: 03-room-ko-1440.png → 04-contact-ko-1440.png/13-contact-es-1920.png: a room filling the viewport gives way to a thin line and separated type on a flat field.
The first-contact section measures 1414px high at 1440×900 for three short beats.
07-distance-ko-1440.png, 08-time-ko-1440.png, 09-duel-ko-1440.png and 11-envelope-ko-1440.png repeatedly place narrative copy at the left and the artifact at the right.
priority_issues.impact: The factual story is complete and personal, but its middle loses the material richness of the opening, then uses the same composition enough times to make progression feel more mechanical.
priority_issues.fix: Tighten the InterPals beat spacing and compose its existing thread at a more substantial scale. Vary one of the next chapter compositions using the already approved birds, city art or room art; carry their material/lighting cues through the transitions. Keep every approved fact, the initial-rudeness beat and the first-day twelve-hour distinction. Add no fabricated chat.

priority_issues.title: Localized chapter copy needs deliberate line breaks
evidence: 11-envelope-ko-1440.png: the final syllable 어. of 좋겠어. occupies a line by itself in the invitation paragraph.
16-duel-es-1920.png: Entre tantas / personas, / tú y yo. becomes a three-line title while the adjacent room has ample horizontal space.
priority_issues.impact: The Korean sentence visibly breaks mid-word and the Spanish chapter heading gains an unplanned extra line. These make otherwise personal copy look mechanically fitted.
priority_issues.fix: Use Korean word-preserving wrapping and widen/balance the invitation paragraph; give the Spanish duel heading a language-specific width or break so it forms two intentional lines. Preserve the factual wording, the approved Hero composition and original art. Check both desktop sizes after the typography change.

personas.walkthrough: Recognizes the personal gift, follows the story and chooses a game.
red_flags: At p=.28 the couple vanishes before the next scene is established; at .35 the room and cosmos overlap.
Opening/read/together are three adjacent letter invitations whose difference is not evident before interaction; together led to an unavailable-service message in this local session.

personas.walkthrough: Uses the labeled gallery controls and range slider, then signs via an available text fallback.
red_flags: Small dark inactive game sculptures are visually weak targets, although the text choices provide a usable alternative.
Small muted supporting labels on the dark story field are less comfortable than the main prose; no quantified contrast or real screen-reader pass is claimed.
working_evidence: Range Home+ArrowRight updated both cities and previous-day label.
Typed name alternative is available beneath the drawn signature instructions.

personas.walkthrough: Enters optional shared opening, signs, folds/rereads, saves a local feedback note and follows the actual game CTA.
red_flags: Together-opening advertises an optional service that was unreachable locally; continue-alone and Escape recovered.
The three-letter-entry labels need to distinguish visual opening, direct reading and synchronized opening more clearly.
working_evidence: Drawn signature reached ready then signed.
Rose reached received; reread reopened the letter.
Local note saved with a visible success message.
Corrected isolation check confirmed Korean persists through feedback→home→game.

minor_observations: The time picker updates numerical time and day offset correctly, but the city art remains a twilight illustration even at the tested01:00/12:00 preview; do not treat it as an exact astronomical preview.
Feedback is a deliberately quiet light reading/form surface with clear grouping. At1440x900 its submission control falls below the initial viewport, but the form scrolls naturally.
No confirmed task blocker. The local shared-event connection failure is environment evidence, not proof that the deployed service is broken.
questions_for_parent_close: Should the next visual pass focus first on the Hero intermediate space, the game-object scale, or story rhythm?
For that pass, should scope be the four priority issues, the Hero handoff only, or Hero plus gallery?

taste_review.seen_in_one_second: The large couple portrait against a rose-lit cosmic room.
taste_review.idea: A shared world for this particular long-distance couple carries their first conversation into play and a letter.
taste_review.live_thing: Working city-time preview, native game selection and the signed letter/rose sequence.
taste_review.layout_words: hero=full-bleed portrait / B=full-bleed room / InterPals=split thread / distance=split birds / time=split clocks / duel=split room / games=curated orbit / letter-invitation=split envelope / letter=centered paper / ending=split rose / feedback=two-column form
taste_review.caps_notes: Visible three-line Spanish duel heading triggers Taste generic6.5 cap. Approved rich art, rose-gold material, original illustrations, private-gift voice and Hero treatment override generic house-style bans. No stock photography or public marketing structure is recommended. Full mobile exclusion prevents claiming a complete award-jury usability result.
